items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I listen to Phil Schaap every morning. I mean I’ve been listening to “Bird Flight” for I mean I don’t even know how many years, probably thirty years.

ctx.x: The radio — that’s not the first story I’ve heard. I’ve heard really nice variations on your story, people, including myself, that it came through the radio, this like wow, what is that?

Yeah, no, and I still love the radio. I listen to Phil Schaap every morning. I mean I’ve been listening to “Bird Flight” for I mean I don’t even know how many years, probably thirty years. I listen to him every morning. And so he and Phil Schaap and Ed Beach are kind of, you know, they’re on the same plane in terms of, you know, the disc jockey as teacher, the disc jockey is informing, not just playing the music but they look upon what they do as teaching. So it’s very cool. And so the radio is a really powerful…

curious about this music. So I try to instill that in my students. I say you have to be curious, and you have to really try and find it. And now with YouTube and all these on- line sources, I mean the whole history of this music, you can see it. You can see Coleman Hawkins play. You can see Lockjaw Davis play. You can see all these guys play. Benny Carter. I mean we didn’t have that growing up when I was a kid. So to be able to — oh man, that’s like the most beautiful thing, to just turn out your computer and…
